# Copilot Instructions — TaskDirectory

Purpose: give an AI coding agent the minimal, concrete knowledge to be productive in this Flutter repository.

- Project type: Flutter multi-platform app (Android / iOS / Web / macOS / Windows / Linux). Entry: `lib/main.dart`.
- Feature layout: `lib/task/` contains feature folders by task (e.g. `task1_login`, `task2_product`, `task3_notes`, `task4_ml`). Prefer editing/adding code inside these feature folders.

Key patterns and architecture
- App entry: `lib/main.dart` initializes Hive and registers `NoteModel` adapter, then starts a `GetMaterialApp` (uses `get` package for routing/state).
- Local storage: Hive is used (see `hive`, `hive_flutter`, `hive_generator` in `pubspec.yaml`). Model adapters are generated by `build_runner` and registered in `main.dart`.
  - When updating Hive model classes (e.g. `lib/task/task3_notes/data/models/note_model.dart`), run:
    ```bash
    flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
    ```
  - Do not edit generated adapter files directly; edit the source model and re-run the generator.
- State & UI: `Get` (GetX) is used — screens often rely on `Get` for navigation and controllers. `GetMaterialApp` is used in `lib/main.dart`.
- Assets / ML: `assets/ml/food_101_model.tflite` and `assets/ml/food_101_labels.txt` are declared in `pubspec.yaml` and used by the `tflite_v2` plugin. Add new assets to `pubspec.yaml` and run `flutter pub get`.

Developer workflows (concrete commands)
- Install deps:
  ```bash
  flutter pub get
  ```
- Generate code (Hive adapters):
  ```bash
  flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
  ```
- Run app on a device/emulator:
  ```bash
  flutter run -d <device-id>
  ```
- Run tests:
  ```bash
  flutter test
  ```
- Build release artifacts (example Android):
  ```bash
  flutter build apk --release
  ```

Project-specific conventions
- Feature scoping: each task feature lives under `lib/task/<task_name>/` and contains its own subfolders for `data`, `presentation`, and so on. Follow this grouping for new features.
- Model/Adapter names: Hive model classes generally have a corresponding `Adapter()` registered in `main.dart` (example: `NoteModelAdapter()`), so ensure generated adapter classes are available after running `build_runner`.
- Avoid editing files under `build/`, `android/` generated intermediates, `ios/Runner/Generated*`, or plugin `generated/` directories. Those are auto-generated during builds.
- When changing package dependencies, update `pubspec.yaml` and run `flutter pub get`. Prefer explicit versioning consistent with existing file (see current dependency block).

Integration points & notable files
- `pubspec.yaml` — assets and dependencies (see the `assets/ml` entries and tflite dependency).
- `lib/main.dart` — app bootstrap: Hive init, adapter registration, `GetMaterialApp`.
- `lib/dashboard_screen.dart` — app home screen.
- `lib/task/task3_notes/data/models/note_model.dart` — Hive model in current focus; examples of generated adapter usage.
- `test/widget_test.dart` — example widget test; run `flutter test` to execute.

Safety and limits for AI edits
- Small, focused edits are preferred: change one feature or model at a time.
- Run codegen (`build_runner`) after changing annotated models (Hive) — missing adapters will cause runtime errors.
- Do not modify platform-generated files or the CI/build system without explicit human confirmation.

If you make a change that requires manual verification (e.g., adding a native plugin), include clear instructions in your commit message and ask for a human to run the app on target platforms.

Questions for the maintainer (when uncertain)
- Should new features follow semantic versioning in `pubspec.yaml`? (Default: follow repository's current style.)
- Preferred testing threshold for accepting feature changes (unit/widget/integration)?

End of instructions.
